text:
support_ana: Heads up — customers on dedicated pool rp-dedicated-42 are reporting a ~60% throughput drop since 09:20 UTC. High tail latency and intermittent 429s. Customer SRE opened ticket.
jon: I'm on it. Any sample request IDs or logs we can use to repro quickly?
support_ana: req-238a, req-238b. Traces show long enqueue times (~200ms) then tiny batches (1-2 tokens). No auth or billing errors in logs.
elin: quick glance at continuous-batcher metrics: avg batch_size collapsed to ~1.8. p95 enqueue spike. Looks like packing is failing — many tiny batches.
sahil: autoscaler logs show no scale up events after 08:55. Utilization stayed below threshold because batches are tiny, so autoscaler didn't trigger.
maya: who touched per-tenant defaults for rp-* pools this morning?
elin: config audit: commit 7f9e3b0 rolled out at 08:50 changed defaults for max_batch_tokens -> 64 for matching pools. That seems suspicious — previously 1024.
jon: can you paste the affected config snippet?
elin: ```
# infra-config for rp-dedicated-*
pool: rp-dedicated-42
max_batch_tokens: 64
batch_window_ms: 10
scheduler:
  per_request_affinity: true
```
support_ana: Customer wants mitigation now — they see sustained 429s and rising tail latencies.
jon: short-term mitigation: bump max_batch_tokens back to 1024 for rp-dedicated-42 and increase batch_window_ms to 20ms. Also disable per_request_affinity for this pool to allow better packing.
infra-bot: deploybot: rolled config 7f9e3b0 at 08:50 UTC. Initiating rollback to previous config for rp-dedicated-42 in 2m.
elin: applying canary patch to rp-dedicated-42 now. Command I'm running:
```
kubectl -n serving set env ds/batcher POOL_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=1024 --record --selector=pool=rp-dedicated-42
kubectl -n serving set env ds/batcher POOL_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=20 --record --selector=pool=rp-dedicated-42
```
jon: also check metrics endpoint while you deploy: `curl -s "https://infra-metrics.internal/metrics?pool=rp-dedicated-42" | jq '.batch_size_avg, .enqueue_ms_p95'`
elin: deployed canary. Observing metrics — batch_size_avg climbing: 1.8 -> 4.2 after 90s.
sahil: changed autoscaler cooldown for this pool from 10m -> 2m in staging (PR #4823). Long cooldown made it blind to short-term recoveries.
jon: after canary rollout to the pool, avg batch size stabilized ~7.6 and throughput recovered to ~85% of normal within ~6 minutes. Tail latencies dropping. Looks like config was root cause.
support_ana: telling customer: mitigation applied, we're monitoring. They asked why autoscaler didn't add nodes.
sahil: answer: autoscaler didn't see utilization because small batches kept CPU/GPU busy for shorter bursts and utilization metrics are averaged over window tied to batch tokens. With tiny batches we under-report load.
maya: please create incident ticket and postmortem. Assign owners for config guard + autoscaler tuning + customer comms.
jon: assigning owners: elin (root cause + config guard), sahil (autoscaler tuning and cooldown), maya (customer comms & incident doc). I'll file the incident doc and link customer ticket.
elin: proposed permanent fix: add a safety floor that prevents max_batch_tokens < 256 for Dedicated pools and tighten per-tenant override checks. Also add a canary gate for infra-config merges targeting rp-dedicated-*.
jon: agreed. Also add an alert rule that fires on avg_batch_size < 4 for more than 3m for dedicated pools — that'll catch future regressions earlier.
support_ana: customer updated: thanks — latency mostly back, seeing occasional 429 ripples. We'll keep them updated until it's stable for an hour.
infra-bot: alert cleared: dedicated-pool-throttle rp-dedicated-42 at 09:02 UTC.
elin: root cause summary: bad per-tenant default override reduced max_batch_tokens to 64, causing tiny batch packing -> reduced effective throughput -> autoscaler didn't scale due to utilization averaging -> sustained degradation.
jon: remediation checklist: revert bad config (done), apply guard (PR staging), adjust autoscaler cooldown (PR #4823), add alert for batch size, postmortem writeup.
maya: I'll draft the customer summary and link the postmortem when ready. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
support_ana: passing to ops to monitor for 1h then close escalation.
jon: I'll follow up with a quick regression test to ensure config merge pipeline has a validation that flags unusually low batch caps.
elin: also adding a DB of recent per-tenant overrides to make rollbacks faster.
sahil: PRs: #4823 (cooldown), #4829 (batch-floor guard), #4830 (alert rule). Leaving notes in the incident doc.
maya: thanks — closing loop with customer in 30m and will update thread.
